full_judgment: 8. The learned Advocate for the opposite party has also contended that after the order had become effective in view of the operation of the default clause the Court lost his jurisdiction to pass any order which might have the effect of altering or amending the order which has been previously passed. In this connection he has cited the case of Shah Wali Vs. Ghulam Din alias Canaan and another, reported in 19 DLR S.C. 143, same case PLD 1966 Supreme Court 983. In that case it has been held that the provision of section 148 of the C.F.C. under which the Court is empowered to extend the time which may have been fixed by the Court for doing a thing has no application to the case where the words of finality have been used which are capable of operating automatically, bringing the entire proceeding to a termination.
